comments: The delivered sheet redraws the tower in every cell and its stone texture drifts between cells. The importer is run on a prepared sheet (prepare.py in this folder): the tower is cell 1 for every state and each cell contributes only its own fire. Every pixel is a delivered pixel; none is painted or filtered. The original delivery SHA is in provenance.json.
All seven windows are identical, so one scale and one pixel grid register the tower the same in every frame; the source pivot is the tower base centre at the bottom of the window.

The tallest flame (lit-0) sets the shared scale. The shared 75-ink palette has no saturated orange: the flame cores snap to its gold and the outer flame to its red, so flame frames measure below the 0.90 colour-agreement diagnostic against the unquantized sample.
geometry: Collision is one tile and belongs to the rules; art never sets a hitbox. The stage stamps the frame bottom-centre at the tile centre x and one half tile below the tile centre y (the tile foot).
mapping_basis: Visual review of the prepared sheet and the delivered sheet, 2026-10-18. Reading order equals the request order: the cold tower (cold-0), a small flame and a larger flame leaning right (kindling-0, kindling-1), then four large flames: upright, leaning left, short and broad, leaning right (lit-0..3).

pieces.label: cold-0: the tower and iron bowl with ash and two dead coals; no flame.
pieces.name: cold-0

pieces.label: kindling-0: a small flame over two glowing embers.
pieces.name: kindling-0

pieces.label: kindling-1: a larger flame leaning right over the embers.
pieces.name: kindling-1

size_basis: native canvas 24x36, anchor bottom-centre (12,36); stage 384x224 at 16 px per tile; a knight is 16x16; the beacon is a tower and iron bowl more than two knights tall.
timing: cold 12 ticks; kindling 2x6 ticks; lit 4x4 ticks (30 Hz). Art never sets a hitbox (collision is one tile).
